title: Adding Value to Crop Produce
status: draft: written 18 Nov 2026 offline for Grade 7 Agriculture; not yet checked by a CBC Agriculture teacher; not loaded by the live tutor
notes: Make sun-dried sweet potato or cassava chips, or fried crisps (frying by the teacher), and compare the price and shelf life with the raw produce.

skills.key_step: The child names ways of adding value to crop produce (cleaning and sorting, grading, drying, milling into flour, frying into crisps, roasting, packaging and labelling) and says value addition raises price and storage life.
representations: raw and processed samples with prices
steps: Compare price and how long it keeps.

board.do: Write "raw groundnuts: 150 shillings; roasted and packed: 300".

misconceptions.ask: How does value addition help a farmer?
misconceptions.repair: Compare the price of a kilogram of raw groundnuts with roasted, packed groundnuts.
Define value addition: changing produce so it is worth more or keeps longer.

misconceptions.ask: What comes first in preparing produce for sale?
misconceptions.repair: Show crisps made from unsorted potatoes with bad spots; who would buy them?

listen_for: It does not; price is all
misconceptions.ask: How else does drying cassava add value, besides a better price?
misconceptions.repair: Compare a raw cassava root after a week with dried chips.

checks.question: Give a way of adding value to cassava.
checks.answer: drying into chips or milling into flour

checks.question: How does value addition help a farmer?

skills.key_step: The child says the steps of adding value: choose sound produce, clean, sort, peel, slice evenly, dry or fry (by an adult), cool, pack in clean sealed packets, label, then compare with raw produce.

board.do: Write the cards: label, slice, sort.

misconceptions.repair: Pack warm chips in a sealed bag: droplets form inside.

misconceptions.ask: Why are potatoes sliced thin and even for crisps?
misconceptions.repair: Fry or dry thick and thin slices; compare.

misconceptions.ask: Why is a packet of dried pumpkin labelled?
misconceptions.repair: Compare two packets, one labelled and one plain; which would you buy?

misconceptions.ask: Can sweet potatoes with rotten spots be used for chips?
misconceptions.repair: Show chips with dark bitter spots.

checks.question: Why are chips cooled before packing?
checks.answer: warm chips sweat in the packet and go soft or mouldy
